accessibilityPage.lead: We want everyone to be able to use this website, including people with visual, hearing, motor and cognitive impairments. Our target is WCAG 2.2 level AA.
accessibilityPage.panelText: The “Accessibility” button is in the header of every page. In the panel you can enlarge text up to 200%, change spacing, turn on high contrast, the dark or warm scheme and a highly legible font, reduce animation and enable simplified mode. Settings are stored only in your browser.
keyboardItems: Tab and Shift+Tab move between elements; focus is always visible.
The first link on every page is “Skip to main content”.
Enter follows a link; Enter or Space presses a button.
limitsItems: Not every scan of an archival document has a text transcription; when one is missing, this is stated next to the scan.
External route services (maps) follow their own accessibility rules.
Some historical images have low original quality.
accessibilityPage.feedbackText: If something on the site is inconvenient or inaccessible, write to us via the feedback and suggestions form. This is not an official appeal: a reply is not guaranteed, but every message is taken into account when improving the site.

terms.fond: A fonds is a body of records that belong together historically or logically, for example all records of one organisation or one person. Each fonds has a number.
terms.inventory: An inventory is a list of the files in a fonds with their titles and dates. It is used to find the file you need.
terms.case: A file (storage unit) is a set of documents gathered on one matter and kept under one number in the inventory.
terms.sheet: A folio is a numbered page of a file. Folio numbers show where a document is within the file.
terms.archiveCode: An archive reference code is the document's address in the archive: the fonds, inventory, file and folio numbers, for example “F. 1. Inv. 2. File 3. Fol. 4”. You can type a code into the catalog search.
terms.restricted: Restricted documents appear on the site only as a record card with access conditions, without a copy or transcription. Closed documents are not published on the site.
terms.readingRoom: In the reading room you can work with original documents and copies that are not published on the site. The address and hours are in “Branches and contacts”.
terms.digitalCopy: A digital copy is a scan of a document that you can view on the site. Only open documents that have passed checks have one.
